summary: All non-sandbox gates pass (fmt/schema/doc/i18n drift, ts-check, clippy, 282 unit tests, 77 deterministic evals, 4 replay evals). 9 checks fail, every one with the identical root cause: sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted. This is an environment limitation, not a code regression; re-run just check in a plain terminal to confirm.

twoLayerRootCause.environment: Background processes launched by the agent are reaped between conversation turns/compaction. Both dashboard and gateway had exited (logs stopped ~09:19).
twoLayerRootCause.code: HttpTransport treated any SSE drop as terminal: #shutdown set #closed=true, aborted the shared controller, fired onClose -> JeevesClient.#closedReason pinned forever -> every later call rejected with "the connection is gone". No reconnect existed. A single Runtime restart therefore permanently哑ed the long-lived gateway client.

changes: SSE drop no longer fires onClose (client stays usable); only explicit close() is terminal.
Auto-resubscribe with linear backoff (500ms -> 10s cap); healthy stream resets backoff.
Per-request RPC no longer shares the SSE abort controller; 20s completion timeout.
#firstAttempt resolves once, never rejects — a transient startup failure cannot poison requests.
fix.test: Added "An SSE drop reconnects and never closes the client" in packages/client/test/http-transport.test.ts.

taskToolDispatcherFix.userObservation: Bot replied that ls cannot run because the main conversation is read-only and shell execution only happens in a task workspace; it fell back to a read-only directory listing. User flagged a design inconsistency: early non-task messages WERE put into the task area, but this clear command task was NOT treated as one.

rootCause.code: interaction/mod.rs:179-186 — the main conversation only gets the `task` tool when may_dispatch(settings.dispatchers, source) is true. may_dispatch = source.is_none_or(|s| dispatchers.contains(s.sender_id)). For a group message source=Some(sender), so an EMPTY dispatcher list admits nobody -> no task tool -> model cannot dispatch -> stuck in read-only main conversation.
rootCause.configBreak: The Runtime (jeeves-config/src/lib.rs:561) reads dispatchers ONLY from JEEVES_DISPATCHERS. .env had that line commented out (#JEEVES_DISPATCHERS=ou_xxx,ou_yyy), so the list was empty. LARK_DISPATCHERS (added earlier) is read only by the gateway and injected into the Runtime ONLY in stdio mode (bin-lark.ts:65 env:) — but the current setup is HTTP mode (JEEVES_GATEWAY_URL set), so that injection never reached the Runtime. Two sides were out of sync.
rootCause.whyItLookedInconsistent: Private chats have source=None -> may_dispatch returns true -> task tool present -> early DM messages could be dispatched into the task area. Group messages have source=Some(sender) -> with an empty list, no task tool -> this group command could not be dispatched. Same feature, two doors, different tooling.

trueRootCause_envFormat.verdict: The REAL reason the dispatcher fix never worked: a shell source error, not logic/config.
trueRootCause_envFormat.evidence: bash: source .env -> ".env: line 196: JEEVES_DISPATCHERS: command not found"; ${#JEEVES_DISPATCHERS}=0. All prior verification used a Python parser (tolerant of spaces, read 35 chars) AND suppressed source stderr with 2>/dev/null, creating a false "fixed" signal.
trueRootCause_envFormat.cause: Line 196 was written as `JEEVES_DISPATCHERS = ou_...` (spaces around =). shell source does NOT accept KEY = VALUE — it treats it as a command. Sibling vars LARK_ALLOW / LARK_DISPATCHERS used correct KEY=value and loaded fine. So gateway saw the dispatcher but Runtime always saw an empty list.
chain: 1. Runtime source .env -> line 196 fails -> JEEVES_DISPATCHERS empty
2. Gateway LARK_DISPATCHERS loads fine -> tags group msg with source=Some(sender)
4. No task tool on main conversation -> model tries run_command directly -> permissions.rs:148 "the main conversation is read-only"
5. Why it looked inconsistent: DM source=None -> may_dispatch returns true (task tool present); group source=Some -> checks empty list -> false. Only group msgs were broken.

whyMultipleApprovals.verdict: EXPECTED DESIGN BEHAVIOR, not a bug.
whyMultipleApprovals.cause: JEEVES_APPROVAL=on-request + JEEVES_EXEC_ALLOW empty (deny-all) + approval card is approve-once only.
codeEvidence: approvals.ts:35-38 comment: "Two buttons; the answer is once only (remember: once), so a standing rule can never be granted from a group chat."
approvals.ts:66: buttons are only "Approve once" and "Deny" — no always/session option.
permissions.rs:181: ApprovalRequest carries reason "Standard session: confirm this operation once".
permissions.rs:184: remember: None — Runtime never persists a broader grant from this path.
whyMultipleApprovals.mechanics: The model split "run ls" into 3 separate commands (ls -la, pwd && ls, echo ok). Each is a distinct operation, not in the allowlist, so each needs its own one-time approval. Three commands -> three cards -> three clicks.

howToReduceApprovals: Set JEEVES_EXEC_ALLOW to a comma-separated allowlist (e.g. "ls *,pwd,echo *") so matching commands run without asking. Docs: configuration.md:322 / configuration.zh.md:294; max 64 rules, trailing * wildcard, empty=deny all.
Note: a standing rule cannot be granted from a group card by design; it must be set in .env or via the dashboard settings API (config/write), which is intentionally not exposed to chat gateways.

rootCause.verdict: UNDER INVESTIGATION — two earlier hypotheses were DISPROVEN by code reading: (1) NOT an SSE knock vs full-notification mismatch — /api/notifications sends full ServerNotifications (stream.rs:488-501) and http-transport emits them intact; (2) NOT a dead-end EventSink — task execution uses the main stdout sink (task_tool.rs:326 -> dispatch::kick(sink) -> run_turn_inner(&sink)); the drop(receiver) seen in runtime.rs:388 is only the startup-recovery path, unrelated to this group-triggered task.
chain: Task completion calls crate::task::notify(sink, &row, ...) from turn/settlement.rs:288 (and task/mod.rs, contract.rs, etc.).
EventSink::notification does `let _ = self.tx.send(Frame::Notification(...))` — silent on failure (server/events.rs:33-34).
For background/waited tasks, that sink comes from EventSink::channel() whose receiver is immediately drop()-ed (server/runtime.rs:388-390, 405-407). So the send silently fails.
Only the app-server MAIN stdout carries notifications to ops read_loop (client.rs:264-272) → shared.events broadcast → /api/notifications SSE. The dead-end sink never reaches stdout.
Therefore gateway never receives type=taskUpdated, bridge.onTaskUpdated never fires, taskReporter never calls task/get or send -> no report line in Feishu.
supportingEvidence: gateway.log mtime 09:43:01, task finishedAt 09:43:32 local (UTC 15:43:32, host TZ CST-0600) — gateway log silent before the task finished.
gateway has only ONE TCP conn to 7777 (the SSE, fd15 49904). If taskReporter had called task/get (RPC POST), a second short-lived connection would have appeared. None did -> handler never fired.
http-transport.ts onLog is a no-op (line 141), so any transport error is invisible in logs.
rootCause.classification: NOT a Feishu config issue, NOT the dispatcher/.env issue (that is fixed and the task dispatched correctly). This is a notification-routing gap between the long-task engine and the ops SSE bridge.

fixOptions: A. Wire task notifications to the main EventSink: instead of EventSink::channel()+drop(receiver), pass the app-server main event sink into task::notify / waits::arm so taskUpdated reaches stdout -> ops broadcast -> SSE -> gateway. Correct architectural fix.

B. Gateway-side fallback: after a task turn completes, have bridge.ask poll task/get (task id from TurnCompleted meta) and call taskReporter directly — avoids relying on the broken notification path. Smaller change, works around the bug.
C. Accept as known limitation: results are visible in dashboard/task API only; group gets no "Done" line. Document as carry-in.
